title: Scout Lilian
dek: Pristinia’s blunt, practical scout: a guide and wildlife coordinator who grows into wartime responsibility, then dies trying to get a warning home.

facts.Death: Rahu archers acting on Magnus’s direct order

body:
Scout Lilian was a field scout, wilderness guide, and early-warning coordinator for Pristinia. She watched roads, tracked enemies, brought exhausted warnings home, and helped adventurers find the dangers they were strong enough to confront. Her importance came from practical knowledge and professional judgment, rather than extraordinary combat power.

The primary quest logs use Lilian; Scout Lillian and Lillian are alternate spellings. She was killed on 4 June 2025. Herb was later restored to life, but the recovered record does not establish Lilian’s resurrection.

A scout, not a warrior

Lilian could use a bow, stalk through the woods, establish signals, and assess routes. She also knew when observation had become too dangerous. In March 2024 she reported purple-glowing creatures near the ruins and their shadow scouts, then retreated with enough information to warn the town. She did not need complete certainty before bringing an actionable report home.

Fear and exhaustion recur in her scenes. Neither prevented her from returning to the field. Her job was to learn enough, survive, and make stronger allies understand where they were needed. The May 2025 narration explicitly calls her a scout, not a warrior.

From recruit to coordinator

In April 2024, Lilian admitted she was still new and apologized when irritation made her unprofessional. She worked around Rolen Ofandrus’s archery and scouting training, helped prepare defenses, and learned to combine field observation with clear reporting.

By May 2025 she spoke of “my scouts,” verified enemy movements, and tracked several fronts during the Rahu siege. She reported the loss of the road to the Before, allied Ahau engagements, approaching siege engines, and likely arrival windows. She ordered preparations to evacuate Pristinia while leaving the adventurers’ response to their own judgment.

This is for you all to decide. You have your choice, we do not order you.Scout Lilian

Knowledge that kept people alive

Lilian understood roads, bandits, winter sea winds, fog, darkness, and the limits of local travel. She reminded visiting adventurers that Pristinia was a frontier community of a few hundred, whose horses mostly worked rather than waited to carry heroes.

Her expertise extended to magical specimens. During a July 2024 predator hunt she quickly harvested wolf fangs before their magical lifeforce dissipated and explained that useful properties depended on the creature and the body part. Witnesses recognized a professional at work.

She also challenged the information gap between powerful adventurers and ordinary residents. Townsfolk often heard only rumors of missions that affected their safety. Regular debriefs offered a practical way to make knowledge serve the community.

Warnings carried through fear

On 31 May 2024 she returned in tears and out of breath with news of Nienna’s capture, then offered to lead the rescue. Delay mattered because the Rahu could conceal their tracks.

On 6 September 2024, she ran for hours to warn that Eovar was burning under attack by strangers. After witnessing an eldritch worm kill a man, she openly admitted she was not all right. She still supplied the harbor’s location, direction, travel estimates, and the crucial distinction that these attackers were not the enemies Pristinia already knew.

But talking wastes time. The clock forever turns forward.Scout Lilian

A life within Pristinia

  • Melian Starguard was a trusted leader. Lilian respected her scouting orders, resented people who bullied her, and helped arrange a meal to cheer her during the war.
  • Herb accompanied Lilian on that final visit. The record supports this act of shared care without inventing a lifelong intimate friendship.
  • Her raven was a working companion and emergency messenger. Its name is not established.
  • Her husband appears in early scenes as the target of familiar, sharp teasing. His name, later fate, and full relationship history remain unknown.
  • Rolen Ofandrus and the adventurers connected her fieldwork to training, defense, and stronger combatants. She informed the adventurers without assuming the right to command them.

4 June 2025: the final warning

Lilian and Herb approached Melian’s hiding place with a special meal. They were visiting a tired friend, not attacking a Rahu force. Magnus Niriin had already led a covert Rahu operation into Pristinia, incapacitated Melian with gas, and prepared her abduction.

Lilian recognized the Rahu and shouted, “Herb! Run! It’s the Rahu!” Magnus ordered that no witnesses survive, then explicitly commanded, “Kill the scout first!” Lilian sent her raven toward home with “Fly! Get help!” and attempted to escape.

Rahu archers acting on Magnus’s direct order shot Lilian in the back and killed her. Herb died moments later. Magnus personally pursued and killed the escaping raven with Eldritch Blast. He did not fire the arrows that killed Lilian; he led the operation, selected her as the first target, ordered her death, and destroyed her attempt to warn Pristinia.

5 June: the bodies become evidence

Investigators found Lilian, Herb, and the raven dead, with Melian missing. Black-fletched arrows were in Lilian’s back and Herb’s front; the raven bore eldritch burns. Fulmin began connecting the burns with Magnus’s known magic. The master record’s directly observed raid and the investigators’ developing deductions are distinct stages of knowledge.

The warning did not escape in time to prevent the abduction, but the bodies and physical evidence allowed the operation to be reconstructed. Lilian’s death damaged Pristinia’s ability to see danger coming as well as ending one person’s life.

The open record

Her husband’s name and fate, the raven’s name, her formal rank, the size of her scout network, its later recovery, and how Pristinia separately memorialized her remain unresolved. No clear source establishes that she returned to life. Her biography preserves the growth from a new recruit to a responsible coordinator without turning her into a secretly powerful warrior.

A sharp tongue and a recruit’s correction

Lilian’s early scenes have a much sharper tongue than a formal scout report. She teases her husband’s inability to sneak, complains about him to Rolen and jokes darkly when asked whether he should help with lumber. When she is corrected, she acknowledges being unprofessional and says she is still new to the job. The exchange preserves both her temper and her willingness to accept training.

She comes looking for Quake because a farmer has agreed to supply fertilizer and cured lumber for his work. Agricultural supplies, draft horses and defensive building compete for attention. On the journey afterward she slips into the fog, circles the area and reports through predetermined signals. Her local knowledge is useful before she becomes responsible for a larger scout network.

A frightened elk and hunters who need watching

When a frightened elk runs into Pristinia, Lilian has no scouts free to handle it and calls for help. She is relieved when the adventurers resolve the situation without hurting the animal and offers drinks at the tavern. She reports a longer pattern of wildlife venturing out and becoming aggressive, but does not know the cause. Her suggestions about contamination and a recent frightening apparition remain possibilities she discusses, not a settled explanation.

Later she asks another party to watch Simon and his friends as they hunt changed animals. She is exasperated by his swagger but does want the harmful creatures culled; the request is to keep the young hunters safe, rather than stop the outing altogether. When pressed for a precise account of strange effects after the animals die, she admits that reports differ. Uncertainty is part of the warning she gives.

A raven’s work and the limits she sets

Her raven also scouts independently. When it finds a logging camp reduced to a bloody scene, Lilian recruits help and offers the bird as a guide while she attends to work for Melian. The companion is part of the town’s working network long before its final attempted warning.

When her scouts report possible Death worship near the Gate, Lilian does not pretend to be an expert in it. She guides the adventurers toward the reported site and rejects the idea that she should take on their larger war herself. Her concern is Pristinia and its people. The boundary can sound curt, especially when she and Navi irritate one another, but her account also clearly marks what she has seen, what her scouts report and what she hopes the adventurers will discover.

What the investigators could know

The later investigation’s narrator explicitly places it on the preceding day, soon after the deaths were discovered. That posting boundary does not create an extra day between the raid and the search. The field, open door, missing Melian and three bodies come first. The direction of the arrows and the raven’s eldritch burns then supply more specific evidence.

Oya initially says she is unsure whether Magnus participated. The witnesses to the aftermath do not begin with the complete account available to a reader of the raid. The investigation and the established account of Magnus’s orders therefore remain separate stages of this history.

sections.title: A sharp tongue and a recruit’s correction

evidence.label: Quest scenes & attributed accounts
evidence.summary: The early quest preserves Lilian’s abrasive humor, explicit correction, practical help for Quake and actual signaling work. Her husband’s shortcomings are her characterization, not an independent assessment of his whole life.

evidence.summary: Direct quest scenes establish an unharmed elk, Lilian’s thanks and the later protective assignment. She explicitly lacks a definite explanation for the changed wildlife.
